messages.subject: Inconsistencies in MatchIt output?
messages.body_plain:
Hello:

I am running CEM as a pre-processing step and want to use the matched data in further analyses. In looking at summary statistics for the matched data, I noticed that the control means differ from the MatchIt summary output. For example, using the lalonde dataset:

library(MatchIt)
library(doBy)
data(lalonde)

m.out <- matchit(treat ~ age + educ + black + hispan + married + nodegree + re74 + re75, data = lalonde, method = "cem")
summary(m.out)

#Means given as part of MatchIt summary output:
 


 
 
 
 Summary of balance for matched data: 
  
 Means Treated Means Control 
  age 21.5441 21.1781 
  educ 10.2941 10.3827 
  black 0.8676 0.8676 
  hispan 0.0588 0.0588 
  married 0.0441 0.0441 
  nodegree 0.6176 0.6176 
  re74 456.1345 622.874 
  re75 350.6728 520.7135 
 

m.dat<-match.data(m.out)
summary<-summaryBy(age + educ + black + hispan + married + nodegree + re74 + re75~treat, data = m.dat, FUN = function(x) { c(Mean=mean(x)) } )

#Means extracted from matched data:
 


 
 
 
 treat 1 0 
  age.Mean 21.54412 19.62821 
  educ.Mean 10.29412 9.717949 
  black.Mean 0.867647 0.6025641 
  hispan.Mean 0.058824 0.1025641 
  married.Mean 0.044118 0.07692308 
  nodegree.Mean 0.617647 0.7564103 
  re74.Mean 456.1345 609.6082 
  re75.Mean 350.6728 464.2215 
 

The means for the controls are not consistent with the MatchIt summary output. Does anybody know what is going on here? Thank you for any help,

Christina Locke

messages.subject: Re: confirm d227c2220c6a4885d7e8c25f6e00a31d196275db
messages.body_plain:
The issue you have is that R is case sensitive and, like all programming languages, is very specific about variable names, etc.

So in this line:

> m.out <-matchit(treatment ~ Gender + Ethnicity + PreSS + PrePL + PostSS, data = data4, method = "optimal")
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'treatment' not found

You need to just have it be:
m.out <-matchit(Treatment ~ Gender + Ethnicity + PreSS + PrePL + PostSS, data = data4, method = "optimal")
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'treatment' not found

since "Treatment" has a capital T in your data set.

This line of code should give you your 101 matched pairs.  See the JSS paper I sent then for more details on what to do after the matchit command, including checking balance, getting the matched data, and running the outcome models.

You can also type :
demo(lalonde)

in MatchIt to see a full set of code running matching using MatchIt.

Liz
